snippets.output: An elevated CSF cell count indicates inflammation or infection in the central nervous system (CNS). The absence of red blood cells (RBCs) in the CSF makes subarachnoid hemorrhage less likely.
The low glucose level (49 mg/dL) in the CSF suggests bacterial or fungal infection, as glucose is typically consumed by pathogens.
The elevated protein level (55 mg/dL) indicates inflammation and infection in the CNS.
The raised intracranial pressure (150 mmH2O) may result from inflammation or infection in the CNS.
Ceftriaxone is a third-generation cephalosporin effective against Streptococcus pneumoniae and Neisseria meningitidis, which are common causes of bacterial meningitis.
Vancomycin is added to cover for resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae and other gram-positive organisms.
Supportive care, including fluid management and management of raised intracranial pressure, is essential.
